title: ROI-SSIM guided framework for 3D knee MRI reconstruction under artifact degradation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《ROI-SSIM guided framework for 3D knee MRI reconstruction under artifact degradation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · para0010】Motivated by these limitations, this study proposes a region-aware MRI reconstruction framework based on a 3D Vision Transformer autoencoder guided by a Region-of-Interest Structural Similarity (ROI-SSIM) loss. By explicitly prioritizing diagnostically relevant anatomical regions and evaluating performance under realistic artifact degradation, the proposed framework aims to improve the clinical relevance and robustness of MRI reconstruction.

【Background · para0006】Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a widely applied clinical method for non-invasive diagnosis of abnormalities, providing high-resolution three-dimensional views of internal anatomy [1]. In this modality, image formation depends on radiofrequency (RF) signal emissions during tissue relaxation, which encode anatomical information [2]. Consequently, this inherent dependence on precise spin alignment and signal acquisition makes MRI particularly sensitive to external disturbances: even slight motion, fluctuations in field homogeneity, or local susceptibility differences can violate the assumptions of spatial encoding and introduce artifacts [3,4].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《ROI-SSIM guided framework for 3D knee MRI reconstruction under artifact degradation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Experimental setup and evaluation protocol · para0038】Reconstruction quality was evaluated using SSIM, PSNR, and NMSE, computed according to the fastMRI evaluation protocol. Metrics were calculated slice-wise and averaged at the volume level. Region-specific fidelity was assessed using the proposed ROI-SSIM, computed within annotated anatomical regions. Unless otherwise stated, reported results correspond to the mean over the validation set. Baseline results were obtained from published validation-set evaluations using the fastMRI knee dataset under the R=4 acceleration setting. No test-server submissions were used. For classical baselines, we report the best-performing configurations under the R=4 setting as provided in the fastMRI benchmark study [13]. Models were trained using AdamW with an initial learning rate of 2·10−4, weight decay of 5·10−2, and β=0.9,0.95. A cosine learning-rate decay schedule was applied over 200 epochs, with a batch size of 4. Gradient norms were clipped at 1.0, and mixed-precision training was used. The output convolution was zero-initialized, and the predicted residual was added to the zero-filled input, such that the initial reconstruction approximated the identity mapping. This residual formulation was used to improve optimization stability during early training. Model checkpoints were selected according to validation ROI-SSIM. All experiments were implemented in Python 3.11 using PyTorch 2.10.0 with CUDA 13.0 and were performed on a single NVIDIA A100 80 GB GPU.

【Experimental setup and evaluation protocol · para0037】Quantitative evaluation was restricted to the validation subset because ground-truth reconstructions for the test set are not publicly available. Experiments were conducted under the R=4 Cartesian undersampling configuration, the most commonly reported setting in the fastMRI literature. Zero-filled inverse Fourier reconstructions served as network inputs.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《ROI-SSIM guided framework for 3D knee MRI reconstruction under artifact degradation》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Quantitative results on clean validation data · para0040】Table 1 reports quantitative reconstruction performance on the fastMRI validation set under the R=4 undersampling condition without additional simulated artifacts. Among the listed methods, the proposed ViT-AE achieves the highest SSIM, although its PSNR is lower than that of the published U-Net baseline. Compared with the baseline ViT-AE trained using only global loss functions, the incorporation of ROI-guided supervision produces a modest improvement in global SSIM. Specifically, ROI-L₁ increases SSIM from 0.819 to 0.820, while ROI-SSIM further improves SSIM to 0.823. These results indicate that emphasizing diagnostically relevant anatomical regions during training does not degrade overall reconstruction quality and may provide measurable benefits in structural fidelity. Among the proposed variants, ROI-SSIM achieves the highest global SSIM while maintaining comparable PSNR and NMSE values. The consistent improvement over ROI-L₁ suggests that structural similarity is a more effective region-aware supervision signal than pixel-wise regional penalties alone, supporting the use of perceptual region-based objectives for MRI reconstruction.

【Quantitative results on clean validation data · para0041】For context, Table 1 includes results from established reconstruction methods. These values were taken from the cited studies rather than reproduced under the present training pipeline, and the global metrics do not rank the methods consistently: the proposed model attains a higher SSIM than the published U-Net baseline (0.823 vs. 0.815) but a lower PSNR (32.4 vs. 34.01 dB). Global metrics alone are therefore insufficient to establish the benefit of region-aware supervision; they average reconstruction quality over the entire image volume and may underrepresent changes within small but diagnostically important anatomical structures. Accordingly, the effect of ROI-SSIM is assessed below through the controlled comparison with the global-loss ViT-AE, followed by analyses of region-specific fidelity and robustness under artifact degradation.

【Fig. 1 · fig0001】Fig. 1 Representative artifact simulations for a single-coil coronal proton-density (PD) knee MRI. (a) Clean reference image with annotated regions of interest; (b) chemical-shift artifact; (c) Gibbs ringing; (d) metal-induced susceptibility artifact; (e) R=4 undersampling; (f) partial-Fourier acquisition; and (g) wrap-around artifact. Absolute difference maps relative to the clean reference are shown below each degraded image, with the corresponding mean absolute error (MAE) and maximum absolute error.

【Fig. 2 · fig0002】Fig. 2 Region-aware 3D Vision Transformer Autoencoder (ViT-AE) architecture for knee MRI reconstruction. ROI-SSIM supervision is applied using ACL, meniscus, and cartilage region masks to prioritize diagnostically relevant anatomical structures during reconstruction.

【Fig. 3 · fig0003】Fig. 3 Ground-truth knee MRI slice with fastMRI+ annotations used to generate volumetric ROI masks for ACL, meniscus, and cartilage supervision.
